findings.exact_text: the line from the trunk was still clipped to his harness, dragging him down with it
findings.reason: Line was anchored to the near trunk, which was already failing, so cutting it would not free him from a falling bridge. Mechanics are muddled.

findings.exact_text: They reached the bridge too late; its far anchors had already torn loose.
findings.reason: Far anchors torn loose, then bridge hangs from near anchor, then bridge 'could no longer carry them' yet Arda crosses it; redundant and inconsistent causality.

findings.exact_text: Their gliders still lay near the old knotted trunk, Arda's tilted where it had been left, both of them safe.
findings.reason: Nisa's glider landing is never shown; also the route line was removed from the trunk. Glider was left tilted after the line was removed, but 'safe' is unsupported.

findings.exact_text: looking at the cut end still in his hand
findings.reason: He had been cutting the line from his harness, but Nisa held the other end; having a cut end in hand is inconsistent with falling and lunging for her wrist.

findings.exact_text: Across the bridge, he reached a cliff edge
findings.reason: Bridge crossing then return puts the camp and bridge relationship confused; the camp is reached after the cliff, yet the bridge is crossed on the way back from the camp.

findings.exact_text: He anchored it to the last living trunk, swung the free end across the gap
findings.reason: Arda anchors the line on his side and Nisa crosses; then he crosses on a collapsing bridge, but later the line is attached to the near trunk, unclear geometry.
Ten minutes is promised but Nisa's return and the camp trek unfolds with unclear timing; corridor dimming 'faster than expected' is not anchored.

findings.exact_text: Somewhere behind them, back past the shore, the corridor they'd flown through was, presumably, still open.
findings.reason: Stormbreak Watch corridor details are fine, but 'cloud wall closing from far side' and shifting positions blur canon of wall as menacing weather only.

findings.exact_text: She came out of it grinning at him from ten meters away
findings.reason: Metric unit in a fantasy sky world is slightly off-register.

findings.exact_text: "Worth it," he said, though it still stung.
findings.reason: Dialogue attribution is jammed in the same paragraph as Nisa's speech; awkward speaker switch.
Interrupted speech after narration beat; 'deal' is not yet established as a deal, awkward.

findings.exact_text: he cut the line away from his harness and gave up the bridge and the rope with it.
findings.reason: Spine has Arda swing Nisa across then cut the line to free himself; cutting is a sacrifice but story muddles what the cut achieves.

findings.exact_text: "The bridge is straining; we have to hurry," he said.
findings.reason: Bridge strain is asserted before they have returned to it, with no basis; then they arrive to find it collapsed, making the statement odd.

findings.exact_text: half a step ahead on the things that mattered
findings.reason: “Ahead on the things” is an unnatural collocation; English normally uses “ahead when it came to” in this construction.
“Were his find” sounds compressed and unnatural here; stating that he discovered the knots is clearer and more idiomatic.
This measure phrase is unnaturally compressed. “Three-quarters of the way across” is the ordinary, immediately clear English expression.
